proposals.evidence: Relaxed database searches yielded unrelated washing, making and speech words rather than a verified ash etymology. None supplies adequate semantic and phonological evidence for a link.

The Rajasthan survey grammar compares suglo/huglo with dirty, and the Mewari dictionary has hugalvāḍo ‘dirt’ (p.364). This establishes a local semantic family, but not its deeper etymon; it must be kept separate from sagal ‘all’.

The Mewari dictionary uses gābā for clothes, confirming that the gloss is not itself anomalous. Database matches in the garbha family refer to pregnancy or an interior and do not establish this clothing word’s ancestry.

Existing regional bāiro/bairā ‘woman’ attestations support comparison, but are themselves unlinked. Similar-looking wind and outside entries belong to different semantic families and are not usable ancestors.

Mewari phoro ‘small, short’ is explicitly attested on dictionary p.238. Database suggestions involving small holes or boils merely share a gloss fragment; they do not establish a historical relationship.

Turner’s jaḍa family includes Konkani ‘heavy’, but the separate ā remains unidentified in this elicited response. Linking only jaḍo would leave the first element unexplained; no whole-response simplex edge is proposed.
